Should You Buy Tesla Stock Before December?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (811 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.
  • Recent findings suggest that tesla (TSLA -1.18%) has had a challenging year.
  • Recent findings suggest that tesla's CEO, Elon Musk, now leads two publicly traded corporations, the other being Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%), which went public in June.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Tesla ›.

Recent findings suggest that tesla (TSLA -1.18%) has had a challenging year. Despite its core electric vehicle (EV) business often performing better than expected, partly due to soaring oil prices, the firm's shares have significantly lagged broader equities. However, the year isn't over, and there is a chance Tesla could finish 2026 with a bang, given ongoing developments. With that said, should investors consider buying the stock before December?

Recent findings suggest that tesla's CEO, Elon Musk, now leads two publicly traded corporations, the other being Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%), which went public in June. Rumors of a potential merger between Tesla and SpaceX have been circulating since before SpaceX was public, but a comment Musk made during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call added fuel to the fire.

Recent findings suggest that musk mentioned that SpaceX and Tesla have formed independent special committees to discuss a potential merger between the two corporations. And more recently, five board directors from both companies have reportedly been discussing a potential all-stock merger that would make the combined entity worth about $3.5 trillion, with a deal possible by year-end. Importantly, this hasn't been confirmed by either company. But it's still worth figuring out the potential benefits and risks of this proposed acquisition.

Recent findings suggest that suppose SpaceX acquires Tesla at a 20% premium in an all-stock deal: SpaceX would have to glitch a substantial number of latest shares, thereby significantly diluting existing shareholders. Tesla's stock might rise, at least initially, while SpaceX's could decline unless investors believe the merger will generate enough synergies to justify the acquisition premium.

Industry observers note that there are indeed some reasons to think that the combined entity could create more value than either would on its own. For instance, both Tesla and SpaceX are investing massive sums in artificial intelligence (AI). As a single entity, they could eliminate redundant investments and lower costs, while leveraging their larger size to negotiate better deals with suppliers.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Recent findings suggest that also, some of Tesla's work, including its energy infrastructure and the Optimus humanoid robot, could be of immense value to SpaceX. So, that could be good news for the business' long-term prospects, although whether the proposed combined entity will, on balance, create more value is by no means guaranteed. However, one major source of uncertainty will likely come from regulators. The deal will probably attract significant attention from lawmakers, at least some of whom may try to stop it.

It has been revealed that whether they succeed or not, it's hard to predict the impact on Tesla and SpaceX. And even as a combined entity, the firm will be significantly exposed to regulatory risk across businesses such as space launch, satellite-based connectivity, EVs, and robotaxis.

Recent findings suggest that putting aside the acquisition talks, Tesla's own business has somewhat attractive prospects. The company's work in the robotaxi industry looks promising. Tesla rolled out the Cybercab, a self-driving vehicle with no steering wheel, no pedals, and no mirrors, earlier this year. Provided it can scale its Cybercab fleet and capture a decent share of the market over the next five to 10 years, the robotaxi business could meaningfully contribute to the company's revenue and profits.

Industry observers note that and Tesla does have an advantage over other robotaxi leaders. The company has a growing number of subscriptions to its Full Self-Driving software, which it offers to EV owners for $99 per month. A growing FSD ecosystem grants the company access to more data to train and improve its software. And as Tesla has pointed out, the FSD software is becoming one of the reasons people buy Teslas. That's great news for the company's future.

But one of Tesla's problems is valuation. At 157.3x forward earnings, the market has already priced in significant success from the manufacturer's robotaxi ambition. So, I'd be skeptical about buying Tesla's shares at current levels. I'd prefer a much lower price. The potential merger with SpaceX changes very little, in my view, and actually adds significantly more uncertainty to the mix.

The combined entity (if a merger does happen) will certainly be worth serious consideration, but investors with an average tolerance for risk and volatility shouldn't buy Tesla stock right now, whether or not they expect the organization to merge with SpaceX.

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:27PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than FreightCar America ›.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 10, 2026, FreightCar America (RAIL +4.39%) reaffirmed its full-year revenue guidance of $370 million to $410 million despite lower quarterly railcar deliveries. The business isn't relying solely on newly introduced railcar manufacturing. Expanding aftermarket sales and internal cost cuts could position the manufacturer for profit growth when railcar demand rebounds. Three things management stated stand out.

Sources indicate that freightCar America acquired three aftermarket suppliers within a year, the latest after quarter-end. Organic parts growth and earlier deals boosted third-quarter aftermarket revenue by 65% year over year to $10.8 million with a 44.5% gross margin. This segment generates repeatable revenue that cushions cyclical drops in new railcar orders.

Industry observers note that the company expanded its market share in addressable latest railcar orders over the trailing 12 months while protecting its pricing discipline. This commercial momentum lifted total backlog value by 28% year over year to $284.5 million.

Management completed a workforce realignment in the second quarter that delivers about $12 million in annualized structural cost savings. The savings reduce fixed overhead without cutting manufacturing capacity. This operational setup could create operating leverage for the anticipated industry replacement cycle.

It has been revealed that railcar storage levels are falling across North America as shippers bring railcars back into service. The manufacturer maintains flexible production lines, expands aftermarket distribution, and reduces structural overhead, aiming to capture margin gains as order volumes rise.

Commercial focus remains tied to pricing discipline and customer retention across major railroads and industrial shippers rather than chasing low-margin volume.

#143610. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (754 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
  • In a recent development, huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the manufacturer.
  • According to recent reports, nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

In a recent development, huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the manufacturer. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

According to recent reports, nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

"Although we expect the manufacturer to fulfill all of its previously confirmed commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said in a note Thursday.

The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

Tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

Industry observers note that on Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

According to recent reports, it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The firm had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

Industry observers note that coreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, remarked CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

"We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.

"However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

Recent findings suggest that "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my organization every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he remarked in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

It has been revealed that bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any big changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

The real glitch is just how much money the organization will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

Sources indicate that "Big companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he said. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

— CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

Prediction: These 3 Consumer Stocks Will Beat the S&P 500 Over the Next 10 Years

  • When I look for that kind of staying power in the consumer world, I aim for three things: a brand that people pay up for, a long expansion runway, and a management team that protects both.
  • Ferrari (RACE +2.96%) deliberately builds fewer cars than people want, and that scarcity is the heart of its economic moat, which is a durable advantage that keeps rivals from stealing its customers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Micah Zimmerman – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:30PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Ferrari ›.

In a recent development, beating the S&P 500 sounds simple until you remember how good the index already is, since it has compounded at about 9.9% a year on a total return basis going back to 1928. So a stock that beats the index over 10 years needs more than a good quarter, it needs a business that can keep growing over the long term.

When I look for that kind of staying power in the consumer world, I aim for three things: a brand that people pay up for, a long expansion runway, and a management team that protects both. Here are three consumer stocks that I think long-term investors should consider for the decade ahead.

Ferrari (RACE +2.96%) deliberately builds fewer cars than people want, and that scarcity is the heart of its economic moat, which is a durable advantage that keeps rivals from stealing its customers.

CEO Benedetto Vigna said in the third-quarter release that deliveries "reflect our clients' ever-deepening desire to make each Ferrari uniquely their own." Those personal touches add profit to every car without adding volume.

In a recent development, demand isn't the problem. Vigna said on the call, "We continue to experience a healthy demand across all geographies, with an order book that enters 2028.".

The risks are a premium valuation, at roughly 36 times earnings, and the shift to electric models like the Luce, which has to win over buyers who love engines.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

According to recent reports, hilton (HLT +0.52%) mostly doesn't own its hotels; it collects fees by managing and licensing its brands to owners through a franchise model, which is an arrangement where a business pays to use another manufacturer's brand and systems. That lets it grow without spending heavily on buildings.

CEO Chris Nassetta noted in the third-quarter release, "We achieved our highest quarter ever for organic openings." He also said on the call, "Globally, Hilton is still less than 6% of supply providing a long runway for continued growth.".

Travel is cyclical, though. CFO Kevin Jacobs remarked, "RevPAR in China declined 5.4% in the quarter," referring to revenue per available room, which is a key hotel measure of how well rooms are filled and priced. Middle East conflict is weighing on that region, too, and the stock trades near 49 times earnings.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

It has been revealed that amer Sports (AS +2.56%) owns Arc'teryx jackets, Salomon shoes, and Wilson tennis gear, and every segment grew by double digits in its latest quarter. CEO James Zheng said, "I am very confident in the future outlook for our manufacturer".

It has been revealed that the U.S. opportunity is what excites me most. Arc'teryx CEO Stuart Haselden noted that the brand has about as many stores in the U.S. as in Canada, which he stated "makes it very apparent the potential that we have to expand in the U.S." Management also said Europe's store traffic is a challenge, and higher freight costs are nibbling at margins.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

It has been revealed that none of these companies will beat the market every year, but I think long-term investors should consider owning all three and giving their growth stories the full decade they deserve. Great brands tend to compound quietly.

What ties these three together is pricing power, which is the ability to raise prices without losing customers, and I think that matters more over a decade than any single quarter's results.

Ferrari's buyers wait years for their cars, Hilton's owners keep signing up for its brands, and Arc'teryx shoppers happily pay premium prices for gear that lasts.

Recent findings suggest that there will be rough stretches, whether it's a travel slowdown, a weak luxury market, or a cold winter for outdoor sales, but investors who hold through those dips give each business time to prove its case. In the end, patience is the edge most investors give up too easily.

  • That same day, President Trump was on a phone interview with CNBC and took credit for speaking with Nvidia's board and helping convince them to bring Huang back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Foelber – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:30PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

In a recent development, nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) investors have been on a rather unenjoyable roller coaster in recent weeks. And every time the ride looks like it's nearing an end, there's another unexpected turn that unearths more questions than answers.

Recent findings suggest that founder and CEO for over 33 years, Jensen Huang, admitted on Nov. 8 to being unfaithful to his wife, then resigned on Nov. 12, only to be brought back as CEO less than two weeks later on Nov. 23.

That same day, President Trump was on a phone interview with CNBC and took credit for speaking with Nvidia's board and helping convince them to bring Huang back. Trump noted, "I spoke to them. Let me just put it that way. And I convinced them. And I will tell you, it was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week and a half ago." Trump was referring to Nvidia's stock price and how it was easier to convince Nvidia to bring Huang back when the stock was cratering.

Nvidia has rallied substantially since Huang came back as CEO, but Huang and Nvidia still face an uphill climb of federal, state, and internal investigations linked to Nvidia misleading investors and potential national security violations regarding advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence (AI) chips leaking into China through backdoor channels.

The stock is still under $100 per share at the time of this writing and down 20% year to date -- making it the worst-performing "Magnificent Seven" stock in 2026. The Magnificent Seven consists of seven mega-cap tech-focused companies that include Nvidia, Apple (AAPL +0.43%), Microsoft (MSFT -1.25%), Alphabet (GOOG -2.02%) (GOOGL -2.13%), Amazon (AMZN -3.12%), Meta Platforms (META +3.40%), and Tesla (TSLA -1.18%).

Here's the simplest reason to buy Nvidia, and an argument for why it's best to keep the semiconductor stock on a watch list for now.

Recent findings suggest that heading into this year, some investors were concerned that Nvidia would be unable to maintain its breakneck revenue growth rate and high gross margins. But hyperscalers continued to ramp up AI capital expenditures. And Nvidia has broadened its customer base to other enterprises, AI start-ups, AI labs, and neoclouds.

As a result, Nvidia's earnings growth began outpacing its stock price growth, compressing its valuation. But then the unthinkable happened.

It has been revealed that nvidia's stock price has plummeted despite exceptional results and guidance for 75% revenue growth in fiscal 2028. Nvidia reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 17, with revenue more than doubling from the third quarter of fiscal 2026. In the nine months ended Oct. 25, 2026, Nvidia generated $183.3 billion in net income compared to $77.11 billion for the nine months ended Oct. 26, 2025.

It has been revealed that nvidia is on track to surpass Alphabet as the world's most profitable firm. It now trades at just 15.4 times forward earnings -- making it the cheapest Magnificent Seven stock despite having the highest gross margins and the fastest revenue growth rate.

TSLA PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

For context, the forward P/E of the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%) is 17.3 -- meaning Nvidia is now priced like a value stock.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Sources indicate that buying high-quality companies on sale is an excellent way to compound wealth over time. Nvidia doesn't have to deliver blowout results to impress investors. In fact, its growth rate could fall substantially, and it would still be a steal at current levels.

The issue isn't Nvidia's valuation -- it's investors' concerns about where the company could be headed over the next three to five years.

Jensen Huang's sudden resignation exposed Nvidia's extreme vulnerability to key-person risk, governance failures, and an incapable board of directors. Going forward, Nvidia will need to change its structure to be less dependent on Huang, which could make it more rigid and less innovative but also protect long-term investors.

In a recent development, in addition to Nvidia-specific challenges, there's also the risk that AI spending could decline considerably due to higher interest rates, which have made borrowing more expensive. With democrats taking control of the Senate and the House, there may be higher regulatory hurdles to accelerating data center construction. And there's the ongoing risk that compute demand will taper off as AI models become more efficient.

It has been revealed that granted, Nvidia is incredibly well positioned to endure a slowdown because of its industry-leading position and rock solid balance sheet. But it could also lead to stagnating or declining earnings in the medium term, which would challenge Nvidia's valuation.

Industry observers note that all told, Nvidia simply has too many unknowns right now. Until investors get more clarity on the findings of the investigations, the company's succession proposal for Huang, and the extent of its governance overhaul, Nvidia remains a hold.

Heading into the newly introduced year, I'd rather buy high-quality Magnificent Seven stocks with a clear runway for future earnings growth like Alphabet, even if its valuation is more expensive than Nvidia's.

Industry observers note that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration cleared the Investigational Upcoming Drug application, or IND, for LB2501, Legend Biotech's in vivo cell therapy that genetically modifies white blood cells directly inside a patient. It's seeing early clinical success, with a 100% overall and complete response rates at dose level 2.

Recent findings suggest that international expansion is accelerating across 20 markets, and updated treatment guidelines favor cell therapy before antibody treatments. Management is keeping a close eye on doctor referral patterns and manufacturing capacity as overseas sales scale up.

#143593. Tech Report: Not Nvidia. Not Micron. If I Could Buy and Hold Only 1 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Semiconductor Stock Through 2030, This Would Be It.

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (876 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Not Nvidia. Not Micron. If I Could Buy and Hold Only 1 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Semiconductor Stock Through 2030, This Would Be It.

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (876 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 10 stocks we like better than Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ›.
  • Sources indicate that for much of the last four years, semiconductor stocks have been some of the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution.
  • Although both companies have attractive long-term growth prospects, competition could complicate their investment narratives over the next several years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adam Spatacco – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:54PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ›.

Sources indicate that for much of the last four years, semiconductor stocks have been some of the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution. While Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) has become the king of AI accelerators, Micron Technology (MU -4.53%) is capitalizing on unprecedented demand for memory chips.

Although both companies have attractive long-term growth prospects, competition could complicate their investment narratives over the next several years. Moreover, as the AI infrastructure landscape evolves, identifying which chip architectures will dominate the market is becoming more challenging.

Fortunately, there's one semiconductor company that stands to benefit from virtually every major development across the AI chip landscape: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM -1.96%).

Between its graphics processing units (GPUs), networking equipment, and CUDA software ecosystem, Nvidia has an exceptionally durable competitive moat. Nevertheless, Advanced Micro Devices is investing aggressively in its Instinct accelerator portfolio, while some of Nvidia's largest customers are developing custom silicon.

Sources indicate that broadcom has emerged as an important partner in the market for application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), most notably through its relationship with Alphabet and its tensor processing units (TPUs). Meanwhile, Microsoft and Amazon are also developing their own chip portfolios, including Maia, Trainium, and Inferentia.

According to recent reports, another potential source of competition is Space Exploration Technologies' collaboration with Intel on Terafab. Terafab is Elon Musk's semiconductor manufacturing initiative that could eventually reduce SpaceX's dependence on third-party chip suppliers. Although commercial-scale production remains uncertain, the project underscores a growing appetite for vertically integrated semiconductor solutions.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Micron faces a different set of challenges. While the proliferation of generative AI has ushered in a memory supercycle, memory-intensive applications such as humanoid robotics and autonomous vehicles should introduce additional tailwinds over the next several years.

However, Micron competes against Samsung and SK Hynix in the high bandwidth memory (HBM) market. Furthermore, memory pricing has historically been cyclical, leaving producers vulnerable to fluctuations in supply, demand, and profitability.

While Nvidia and Micron could both continue thriving, there is an alternative way to invest in the semiconductor industry without betting on a particular chip designer or memory manufacturer.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

In a recent development, unlike Nvidia and AMD, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) primarily manufactures semiconductors designed by other companies. Its customer base includes businesses spanning GPUs, custom AI accelerators, smartphone processors, and automotive chips.

Against this backdrop, if Nvidia continues to dominate the AI accelerator market, TSMC benefits. Should AMD start to capture additional market share or custom ASICs become increasingly popular, TSMC still stands to benefit because it manufactures chips across these competing architectures as well.

Industry observers note that interestingly, Taiwan Semi also has exposure to the memory supercycle. While the firm isn't a producer of conventional dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), its collaboration with SK Hynix involves manufacturing logic base dies for next-generation HBM4 solutions.

Recent findings suggest that moreover, TSMC's advanced packaging technologies -- particularly its chip-on-wafer-on-substrate (CoWoS) platform -- play a critical role in integrating AI processors with HBM. As a result, growing demand for more sophisticated memory configurations creates additional markets for TSMC beyond traditional wafer fabrication.

The most compelling aspect of TSMC's competitive positioning is the sheer magnitude of its market share. Industry estimates suggest that Taiwan Semi controls roughly 73% of the global pure-play foundry market. By contrast, the next closest competitor sits at just 6%.

Sources indicate that although TSMC isn't technically a monopoly, its dominance gives it the characteristics of one. The company's manufacturing expertise, technological edge, production scale, and customer relationships are simply too difficult for the competition to replicate at scale.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

During the third quarter, Taiwan Semi generated $46.7 billion in revenue, representing 41% year-over-year growth. Meanwhile, the tech giant's gross margin reached nearly 65%, and its operating margin expanded to about 59%.

TSM Revenue (Quarterly) data by YCharts.

According to recent reports, management expects revenue to reach $53.3 billion in the fourth quarter, implying 58% year-over-year growth. These results illustrate how TSMC's manufacturing scale is translating insatiable semiconductor demand into robust profitability.

Despite these impressive financial trends, Taiwan Semi stock trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 15.7. That valuation profile looks attractive for a business generating this level of growth and profitability while commanding such a dominant market position.

Rather than attempting to identify which chip designer or memory producer will emerge victorious over the next several years, investing in the organization that manufactures many of the industry's most in-demand products looks like a compelling strategy.

TSMC's architecture-agnostic business model, durable competitive advantages, and reasonable valuation make it a compelling semiconductor stock to buy now and hold through the end of the decade.

Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

📅 15 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2850 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.
  • Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.
  • His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand said everything you need to know about this moment...

Aug 22: Hull City vs Manchester United.

Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town.

Sep 6: Everton vs Manchester United.

Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City.

Sep 20: Fulham vs Manchester United.

United’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

Four minutes of added time to be played...

United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

Industry observers note that martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

Sources indicate that more substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

Sources indicate that big chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

Industry observers note that milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

Sources indicate that more changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

Recent findings suggest that manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

According to recent reports, manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by new signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

Wholesale changes on the hour mark...

Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari.

In a recent development, manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

Milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

Sources indicate that manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

Industry observers note that united have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

In a recent development, all square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

Industry observers note that fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

It has been revealed that santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs.

It has been revealed that united have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

Recent findings suggest that shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

In a recent development, carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

In a recent development, A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

Estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

Milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

According to recent reports, united make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

Szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

The players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely new cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

We are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

In a recent development, manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

Recent findings suggest that marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

Carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

Aug 5: AC Milan 1 Inter Milan 1.

At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his upcoming role. He stated: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

“It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

“But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

“Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”.

According to recent reports, welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the substantial ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri noted Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

Recent findings suggest that carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

In a recent development, kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, fresh signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

Industry observers note that on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 10, 2026, Dolphin Entertainment (DLPN -0.18%) announced quarterly revenue of $16 million, an 8.3% increase year over year. The entertainment marketing company expanded operating profitability as agency cross-selling, which is selling services across multiple internal divisions, helped top-line growth outpace core operating costs. Three things management stated stand out.

Revenue grew without relying on acquisitions, outstripping core operating costs, which are baseline expenses needed to run daily operations. Cross-selling, or offering services across multiple internal marketing divisions, drove profitability higher across agency units.

Management expects upcoming structural lease expirations and debt maturities to unlock $3 million in annual free cash flow, which represents cash generated after operational expenses. Furthermore, $127 million in NOLs, or net operating losses that can offset future taxable income, should shield most of those savings from corporate income tax.

Sources indicate that beyond core public relations agencies, management is expanding into commercial ventures, which are equity-backed brand partnerships and content projects. The firm expects to launch four latest commercial ventures in 2027, mostly through its fundraising partnership with DealMaker.

Operating momentum is strengthening heading into the final quarter of 2026 as multi-agency collaborations drive cross-selling between public relations and influencer marketing operations. Management points to multi-agency coordination as a potential driver of earnings growth.

Long-term value creation could depend on executing upcoming venture releases and on disciplined expense management that converts recurring revenue into free cash flow.

Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (575 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).
  • Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in?
  • First, let's remember how we got here.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

(See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

First, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout swiftly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

According to recent reports, zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three crucial forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

Recent findings suggest that the following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

The major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

One key clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

Any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

Recent findings suggest that from here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see new highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

Breaking: 2 Dividend Stocks to Buy in November and 1 to Leave on the Shelf

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (760 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 26, 2026 at 6:25PM EST.
  • Altria's (MO +1.95%) 5.9% yield is very attractive, but don't rush out and buy the stock.
  • Altria isn't at any risk of going bankrupt.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 26, 2026 at 6:25PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Altria Group ›.

Altria's (MO +1.95%) 5.9% yield is very attractive, but don't rush out and buy the stock. You may be better off with McCormick's (MKC +1.67%) 4.1%, or even Procter & Gamble's (PG +0.44%) 2.5%. Here's why two of these stocks could be buys in November, and one is likely best left on the shelf.

Altria isn't at any risk of going bankrupt. And its dividend doesn't look particularly risky, either. For more aggressive dividend investors, it may be worth a closer look given its well-above-market 5.9% yield. However, you have to ask yourself why that yield is so high before you buy the stock.

In a recent development, the answer is that Altria's combustible tobacco business, largely cigarettes, accounted for $5.4 billion of its $6.1 billion in revenues in the third quarter of 2026. That's 88% of the top line, which is a major problem when you consider that the number of cigarettes and cigars the manufacturer sold fell 2.9% in the quarter to 16.2 billion. In the third quarter of 2021, the company sold nearly 24.5 billion, indicating that this is a long-term trend. To be fair, Altria is working hard to diversify its business away from smokeable products, but given the uncertainty in the market today, thanks to geopolitical conflict, inflation, belt-tightening consumers, and AI volatility, why take on that kind of business risk?

At the other end of the risk spectrum is Procter & Gamble, one of the world's largest consumer-staples makers. The company sells paper products, toiletries, and makeup, with its brands typically positioned at the high end of the market. While there is some trade-down risk in that market position, P&G has long focused on leading the consumer staples sector with innovation. The goal is to produce products that consumers are willing to pay more for because they get more from them.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Right now, P&G's 2.5% yield is well above the market's 1% and the consumer staples average of 2%. So you aren't skimping on yield to own this well-run organization. That noted, its price-to-sales and price-to-earnings ratios are roughly in line with their five-year averages, so you aren't getting a bargain price, either. However, given that P&G was able to increase its organic sales growth by a respectable 4% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 despite increasingly cost-conscious consumers, conservative dividend investors should probably give it a closer look.

It has been revealed that mcCormick's risk profile is a bit harder to define, but the risk-versus-reward balance is likely tilted toward reward. The historically high 4.1% yield is a key part of the equation, indicating the stock is cheap today. That's backed up by the P/S and P/E ratios being below their five-year averages. As with Altria, however, you have to ask why McCormick's yield is so high and its valuation so cheap.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

The answer is that McCormick is in the middle of acquiring Unilever's (UL +2.48%) food business. That will roughly double the firm's size and require it to take on significant debt. Those are risks, but the two companies' spice- and flavor-focused portfolios are complementary and offer cross-selling opportunities. And McCormick has a strong acquisition history, including meeting its post-merger deleveraging commitments. If you can handle a little uncertainty for a significant increase in yield, you may want to take a risk on McCormick as November draws to a close. Unlike Altria, whose business is contracting, McCormick's business looks set to get much bigger.

Industry observers note that altria's core business has been in decline for years. While the company has managed to maintain a growing dividend during this period, most long-term dividend investors are probably best off avoiding it. Conservative types would be better off with an industry stalwart like P&G. And if you are willing to take on a little more risk, McCormick's pending acquisition could be an opportunity to buy a historically well-run company while it is attractively priced and offers a well-above-market yield.

    #143558. Industry News: A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (624 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (624 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct.
    • However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive.
    • According to recent reports, buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession plan, makes it worse.

    However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a substantial haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the manufacturer's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

    According to recent reports, buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options. Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

    According to recent reports, this prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

    This lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

    By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    These 2 AI Chip Stocks Are Down 36% to 39% From Their Highs. Here’s What History Says Happens Next.

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (805 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) and Broadcom (AVGO -0.07%) have both taken a beating, with their shares now trading roughly 36% and 39% below their 52-week highs, respectively.
    • With both companies still benefiting from demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, could this sell-off present an opportunity for long-term investors?
    • In a recent development, nvidia remains at the center of the AI boom, supplying the graphics processing units (GPUs), networking equipment, and software that power the world's largest data centers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Rick Orford – Nov 26, 2026 at 7:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) and Broadcom (AVGO -0.07%) have both taken a beating, with their shares now trading roughly 36% and 39% below their 52-week highs, respectively. But history suggests that corrections don't necessarily mark the end of a bull cycle.

    With both companies still benefiting from demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, could this sell-off present an opportunity for long-term investors?

    In a recent development, nvidia remains at the center of the AI boom, supplying the graphics processing units (GPUs), networking equipment, and software that power the world's largest data centers. That remarked, the recent weakness in its share price is notable, given that the company continues to deliver exceptional performance.

    In its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results, Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year. Data center revenue alone reached $107.6 billion, up 110% from the same period a year earlier.

    These results suggest that demand for AI compute infrastructure remains remarkably strong, even as investors become more cautious about how much tech companies are spending.

    Recent findings suggest that and while Nvidia stock trades around 36% below its 52-week high, it has eventually recovered to its previous highs each time. In fact, similar drops in 2020 and 2025 were erased within 56 and 82 days, respectively, of their lows.

    It has been revealed that specifically, across eight recoveries from declines of at least 20%, Nvidia took a median of around 75 days from its trough to regain its previous high. But some recoveries took considerably longer, particularly following the late 2018 sell-off.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    According to recent reports, of course, owning Nvidia stock comes with risks. For one, the manufacturer's recent leadership issues have introduced uncertainty, while U.S. export restrictions and competition from custom AI chips could limit some of its future growth.

    Despite that, at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of just 10 times, Nvidia stock looks modestly priced for a firm still growing revenue at triple-digit rates.

    Meanwhile, the next tech giant is focused on custom chips to drive long-term growth.

    Broadcom is benefiting from a different part of the AI infrastructure opportunity: custom-designed chips and high-speed networking. This is where the manufacturer has established a strong competitive position.

    In practice, Broadcom works with hyperscalers to design custom AI chips and supplies networking hardware to connect complex infrastructure for running AI workloads. Here's how that has shown up in the numbers.

    Sources indicate that in its third-quarter fiscal 2026 results, Broadcom reported revenue of $29.6 billion, up 86% year over year. More importantly, AI semiconductor revenue reached $16.7 billion, representing 221% growth. Management also projected AI semiconductor revenue of $21.7 billion for the following quarter, an increase of 236% from the previous year.

    Right now, Broadcom's shares trade around 39% below their 52-week high. And like Nvidia, they've declined about as much in the past.

    Industry observers note that for example, in the 2022 bear market, Broadcom's shares declined by around 36%; by 48% during the COVID-19 crash; and by 40% during the 2025 tech sell-off. Yet the stock eventually recovered from those downturns. In fact, following its 2025 correction, Broadcom stock finished the year with a gain of about 49%.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Sources indicate that there are still risks to owning the stock. For one, Broadcom faces competition from other custom chip designers, while a slowdown in hyperscaler spending could affect demand for its AI products. These are reflected in the stock's forward P/E of 17 times, which also looks modest given its strong semiconductor growth and solid free cash flow (FCF).

    Nvidia and Broadcom are among the biggest companies in the AI infrastructure boom, but their recent pullbacks raise an key question: Is today's volatility a good buying opportunity?

    Both companies have experienced painful corrections, but their underlying businesses continue to benefit from the ongoing AI build-out. Indeed, history demonstrates that major drawdowns don't necessarily signal the end of a company's bull case. Ultimately, if earnings continue expanding and AI spending remains strong, today's lower share prices could look like attractive entry points.

    As for what comes next, Nvidia could suit value-minded investors, given its lower forward P/E. Broadcom could appeal to those seeking faster AI semiconductor growth and greater upside to analyst targets.

    By Harsh Chauhan – Nov 26, 2026 at 7:08PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Dell Technologies ›.

    Though artificial intelligence (AI) stocks have taken a beating lately, the financial performance of companies in this sector remains solid.

    We have already seen that several AI infrastructure companies, specifically semiconductor stocks, have delivered impressive growth in revenue and earnings this earnings season. And now, Dell Technologies (DELL +0.60%), another key component of the AI data center ecosystem, has delivered phenomenal results.

    Let's take a closer look at Dell's performance and guidance and check why Wall Street is bullish about this tech stock's prospects over the coming year.

    Dell released its fiscal 2027 third-quarter results (for the three months ended Oct. 30) on Nov. 24. The company's revenue jumped by 103% year over year to a record $54.9 billion, well above the $49.3 billion consensus estimate. Dell's non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) increased at a significantly faster pace of 265% year over year to a record $9.45. Wall Street would have settled for EPS of $6.59.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    The incredible demand for the company's AI-optimized servers is behind this stunning performance. The company sold $22 billion worth of AI-optimized servers last quarter, up by 291% from the prior-year period. What's more, even traditional servers and networking equipment were in terrific demand, with revenue from their sales increasing by 235% year over year to $15 billion.

    What's worth noting is that Dell received way more orders than it fulfilled last quarter. Specifically, the firm booked $60.2 billion in upcoming orders for its AI servers, taking its total AI backlog to $132.3 billion. It is worth noting that Dell received $60.9 billion in AI server orders in fiscal Q2 as well, which helps explain why its revenue pipeline continues to improve.

    Recent findings suggest that healthy demand for AI servers has prompted Dell to raise its annual guidance once again. The company now expects 78% revenue growth in fiscal 2027 to $202 billion, higher than the previous estimate of $192 billion. It was originally expecting a 23% increase in revenue at the beginning of the fiscal year, to $140 billion. Even better, Dell now sees its fiscal 2027 non-GAAP EPS jumping by 188% to $29.68, more than double its $12.90 EPS guidance at the beginning of the year.

    Though Dell hasn't issued fiscal 2028 guidance yet, I won't be surprised if the organization sustains its phenomenal momentum next year. That's because Dell already has a massive backlog, pointing to a significant increase in AI server revenue next year. The company is on track to end fiscal 2027 with $78 billion in AI revenue, more than 3x the $25 billion it generated from this segment last year.

    Dell's backlog is likely to increase again this quarter, as the organization notes that its order "pipeline grew sequentially and remains multiples of our backlog." That should set up Dell's AI server business for another year of exponential growth in fiscal 2028 (which ends in January 2028 and overlaps with most of calendar 2027).

    So, Dell stock seems well-placed for another impressive year in 2027 following 125% returns in 2026 as of this writing. That's exactly what Wall Street expects from the stock.

    Dell has a 12-month median price target of $512.50, according to estimates compiled by CNN. That's 72% higher than its current stock price.

    It is easy to see why analysts expect such strong upside from Dell next year. The company is growing at a red-hot pace and has a price-to-earnings ratio of just 12.5, lower than the S&P 500 index's earnings multiple of 20.3. The average earnings growth of S&P 500 companies is expected to be 33% in 2026, and Dell is on track to grow at a significantly faster pace.

    Also, Dell's healthy backlog should help it outperform Wall Street's expectations again next year. It is worth noting that analysts have raised their earnings-per-share estimates for Dell following its latest report.

    DELL EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts.

    Assuming Dell's EPS reaches $32.87 in fiscal 2028 (which ends in January 2028) and it trades at 20 times earnings, in line with the S&P 500's earnings multiple, the stock could jump to $657. That's 117% higher than the current stock price, suggesting that this AI stock could more than double over the next year. As such, buying Dell is a no-brainer right now considering its phenomenal growth and cheap valuation, which should set the stock up for a solid 2027.

    Breaking: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
    • It has been revealed that how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
    • Recent findings suggest that so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

    It has been revealed that how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

    Recent findings suggest that so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

    Sources indicate that title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

    First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

    Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

    It has been revealed that another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

    Industry observers note that “They are really good examples,” Arteta said. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

    “The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

    Industry observers note that you could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

    Industry observers note that it can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

    Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

    You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

    Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

    Recent findings suggest that here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s fresh £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

    Recent findings suggest that when Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

    Sources indicate that it should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

    Industry observers note that city, in contrast to their opponents, revealed a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where latest boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

    Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

    Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

    Industry observers note that throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

    Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

    Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

    Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

    Had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal showed was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

    “I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

    You would be brave to say it will be their last.

I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated.

    A really, really good performance so early in the season. To play at the level we did and the desire we highlighted, I just told them that I really enjoyed watching them.

Shades of 1998 and 2004 when they swept Manchester United aside in this fixture as title winners, only to fail to defend the crown in the season that followed. So maybe it is unwise to make bold forecasts, but it could not have gone better for Arteta. Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis caught the eye, and Arsenal had their usual solidarity defensively. City just completely off the pace, one to write off and move on.
