    #143510. Latest Update: Latin America has the copper and energy the AI build-out needs. Infrastructure is the test

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1164 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Latin America has the copper and energy the AI build-out needs. Infrastructure is the test

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1164 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Latin America’s copper, energy and mineral resources could play a growing role in supplying the global artificial-intelligence build-out, as data centers and electrification drive demand for power and raw materials.
    • But for investors, it's less about whether Latin America has the resources than whether governments can turn them into viable projects.
    • "We are going through an acceleration in energy demand growth.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Latin America’s copper, energy and mineral resources could play a growing role in supplying the global artificial-intelligence build-out, as data centers and electrification drive demand for power and raw materials.

    But for investors, it's less about whether Latin America has the resources than whether governments can turn them into viable projects.

    "We are going through an acceleration in energy demand growth. We need every possible energy source available," Michele Della Vigna, head of natural resources research for Goldman Sachs, told CNBC. "Ultimately, what drives economic growth is energy," he added.

    Ben Kumar, head of strategy for wealth, investment and public policy at 7IM, suggested Latin America could benefit, given the physical materials needed for AI equipment and data centers. "We are at the moment neutral in the short term, but if the materials and mining cycle continues, we could see this moving to positive in a few months," he stated.

    It has been revealed that the investment case varies across the region. Chile has copper; Argentina is expanding oil and gas exports; and Brazil has abundant renewable power and significant rare earth reserves.

    Sources indicate that chile's copper sector illustrates both the supply potential and the constraints to expanding supply. Copper production fell 8.5% in the first nine months of 2026, according to the state copper commission Cochilco, as lower ore grades, maintenance, and operational disruptions constrained supply.

    But demand for refined copper is set to grow 1.6% this year and 2% next year, according to the International Copper Study Group. Supply is struggling to keep pace with demand from expanding electricity grids.

    Sources indicate that chile's copper commission has raised its 2027 price forecast to $5.95 a pound, from $5.10. Codelco, the state-owned copper producer, may also have scope to increase supply, including through proposed public-private partnerships.

    Recent findings suggest that rafael Ch, partner and senior analyst for Latin America and emerging markets at Signum Global Advisors, sees demand continuing to grow. "As countries expand electricity grids, they need more copper regardless of which power source they choose," he said.

    The scale of the opportunity will depend in part on how quickly energy demand grows. Goldman Sachs forecasts that global power demand for data centers will grow by 170% by 2030. The IEA projected in April that global data center electricity consumption would rise from 485 terawatt-hours in 2025 to 950 TWh in 2030.

    The investment case also depends on whether the region can capture more value from the resources it produces. Latin America and the Caribbean refined only 26% of the copper they mined in 2025, according to the IEA.

    "Cautious optimism is justified and there will be massive critical mineral demand," said Monica de Bolle, senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics.

    "But improving refining capacity will be crucial to capture more of that value," she added.

    According to recent reports, some projects have already secured financing. Chilean explorer Marimaca Copper Corp selected a preferred lender for a $400 million debt facility to build a mine on Oct. 28. The funding will go towards developing an open-pit mine in the north of Chile that will produce 50,000 metric tons of refined copper annually. Production is expected from 2029.

    Argentina shows the other side of the opportunity: strong oil and gas resources, but insufficient infrastructure to get more production to global markets.

    It has been revealed that "I see an opportunity in the infrastructure that gets Argentine oil and gas to market. A producer in Vaca Muerta can have excellent wells and still struggle to expand exports without pipeline capacity and access to ports.

    That gives investors a reason to look at transport and export infrastructure alongside production," Rafael Ch, partner and senior analyst for Latin America and emerging markets at Signum Global Advisors, added. Vaca Muerta is Argentina's vast shale basin.

    Sources indicate that argentina is also attracting investment in drilling and export infrastructure. International capital markets have reopened to investment in drilling and pipelines in Argentina. That investment has already driven the build-out of a pipeline and port. Argentina will then be able to export far more crude oil. Chevron and American oil tycoon Harold Hamm have also increased their investments in Argentina.

    In a recent development, brazil's case rests partly on its renewable-heavy power mix. About 89% of the country's electricity was generated from renewable sources in 2025, according to the country's Ministry of Mines and Energy.

    "That puts Brazil in a strong position to benefit as AI and data centers drive up demand," Stephanie Link, chief investment strategist and portfolio manager at Hightower Advisors, told CNBC.

    According to recent reports, but while Brazil has the world's second-largest reported rare-earth reserves, its estimated mine production is far smaller than China's. USGS estimates put Brazil's output at 2,000 metric tons in 2025, compared with China's 270,000 metric tons. Brazil's reserves are estimated at 11 million metric tons by the USGS, second only to China's 44 million metric tons.

    For investors, the gap between Brazil's vast reserves and limited current production is both the opportunity and the execution risk.

    For investors, the policy question is whether governments can make projects viable and keep them on track.

    Luis Costa, Citi's global head of emerging markets strategy, said governments need to offer incentives, particularly in the early stages of projects, because infrastructure lags the region's resource wealth. He also stressed that support must last: infrastructure projects can take several years to develop.

    The World Bank's Latin America and the Caribbean Economic Revision for 2026 projects growth for the region of 2.2%, and highlights the "restricted fiscal space, sticky inflation and high borrowing costs.".

    "The economic policy and fiscal policy needs to get in line as markets are globally becoming more sensitive to fiscal stories," said Costa.

    Brazil will need to establish fiscal credibility to attract investment, particularly if higher public spending puts additional pressure on debt and borrowing costs. "If investors doubt the government can stabilize public debt, companies' long-term financing costs could stay high even as the central bank lowers its policy rate," Ch added.

    In a recent development, with Argentina set for national elections in October 2027, political continuity will also matter for energy investment. "A return to tighter currency controls or persistent deficits would make companies more likely to delay projects, even in an oil field with attractive economics," remarked Ch.

    Pro-business President Javier Milei faces a tight race for re-election, though a change in leadership would not necessarily undermine medium- to long-term investment.

    "There is also the possibility of a pragmatic Peronist ticket emerging, which markets would be satisfied with," said Nicolas Jaquier, emerging-market fixed-income portfolio manager at Ninety One.

    For those governing across Latin America, policies to unlock its wealth of resources will be key for it to emerge as a winner from the AI demand boom.

    "Supply chain security is becoming more and more relevant, and if commodities take off Latin America can be a clear and obvious winner," stated Kumar.

    #143505. Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (510 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (510 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex.
    • With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.
    • Implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting substantial moves.

    With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

    Implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the tech giant that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

    "Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, stated in a text ahead of the firm's after-market report on Tuesday.

    Since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is at the moment 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

    The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

    One catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

    With bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

    By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

    Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

    • Rodgers was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday and was subject to waivers.
    • In a recent development, news broke after 11 p.m.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers passed through waivers on Thursday and was not claimed, according to multiple reports.

    Rodgers was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday and was subject to waivers. After going unclaimed, the quarterback is now free to sign with any team, though it is unclear which teams may be interested given how he conducted himself this week.

    In a recent development, news broke after 11 p.m. ET Tuesday night that Rodgers was not only being benched for the team's Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos, but would also be inactive.

    Sources indicate that rodgers responded by joining "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday afternoon and going scorched-earth on head coach Mike McCarthy for about 35 minutes. The quarterback went off on McCarthy, accusing him of sleeping in meetings, not watching film, and saying, "1-2-3 Packers!" when breaking down a halftime huddle with players.

    It has been revealed that while the writing was on the wall that Rodgers could be headed for a release, his interview with McAfee certainly sealed it. During his appearance, the quarterback even stated he was not going to return to Pittsburgh.

    Recent findings suggest that the soon-to-be 43-year-old is now a free agent. Rodgers could land with a team that has quarterback injury problems or is right on the playoff bubble, but his conduct on Wednesday reportedly means that his options might be even more limited.

    Rodgers may have played the final game of his illustrious career, but his tenure with the Steelers will almost assuredly be remembered for his rant on Wednesday.

    • Nvidia's credit rating could be cut by one notch over the next 90 days if the manufacturer continues to have "deficiencies" in its management and governance framework, S&P Global Ratings said in the wake of the Jensen Huang's ouster and reinstatement as Nvidia CEO.
    • "News regarding the CEO and questions regarding potential export control violations have exposed vulnerabilities in Nvidia's management and governance framework, especially in regard to its board structure, composition, and effectiveness," S&P stated in a Wednesday note.
    • Nvidia right now holds an AA rating, the third-highest level.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia's credit rating could be cut by one notch over the next 90 days if the manufacturer continues to have "deficiencies" in its management and governance framework, S&P Global Ratings said in the wake of the Jensen Huang's ouster and reinstatement as Nvidia CEO.

    "News regarding the CEO and questions regarding potential export control violations have exposed vulnerabilities in Nvidia's management and governance framework, especially in regard to its board structure, composition, and effectiveness," S&P stated in a Wednesday note.

    Nvidia right now holds an AA rating, the third-highest level.

    S&P has placed the chipmaker on "CreditWatch with negative implications," though any potential downgrade would be limited to one notch, to AA-, unless investigations or disclosures lead the agency to conclude that Nvidia's reputation or future prospects have also been harmed.

    Industry observers note that A downgrade can pressure bond prices, push yields higher and raise borrowing costs. Nvidia priced $25 billion of investment-grade senior notes in June, with maturities from 2028 through 2056, shortly after S&P upgraded the firm from AA- to AA.

    Nvidia has about $32.5 billion of bonds in the U.S. high-grade corporate bond index, according to Bloomberg.

    S&P's Wednesday note follows Moody's Ratings changing its outlook on Nvidia to stable from positive on Nov. 18, citing governance concerns, and leaving that outlook unchanged after Huang's return on Monday.

    In its note, S&P cited the "long tenure" of certain board members as a reason their independence may be "compromised" and said Nvidia's management and governance risk was "rising.".

    The ratings agency added that it remained unaware of any remedial action taken by the board to address what could be "meaningful" management and governance deficiencies.

    In a recent development, chairman Harvey Jones and early investor Tench Coxe have served on Nvidia's board since 1993, while Brooke Seawell joined in 1997. Mark Stevens served from 1993 to 2006 and rejoined the board in 2008.

    S&P also flagged questions around geopolitical risk management and internal controls arising from Nvidia's exposure to China.

    "While Nvidia management has delivered significant returns for its stakeholders over decades, weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning have brought questions around the "key man" risk to the forefront," S&P's Andrew Chang and David Tsui stated.

    Chang and Tsui noted that Huang's resignation and subsequent reinstatement did not resolve questions about the board's oversight of executive conduct.

    The agency also intends to meet with Nvidia's board and management to discuss aims to address those deficiencies, particularly around "board independence, effective management oversight and a credible leadership succession initiative.".

    According to recent reports, huang returned less than two weeks after Jones mentioned Nvidia's directors did not intend to reinstate him. The board later voted unanimously to bring Huang back, sending Nvidia shares up as much as 36% during Monday's session.

    Nvidia shares are down about 12.5% since Monday's close.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Wealthy Europeans are looking to alternative asset classes to build exposure to artificial intelligence themes amid turbulence in public markets.
    • According to recent reports, goldman Sachs Alternatives' inaugural survey of high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth investors found 47% of European respondents saw alternatives as the best way to gain exposure to AI and future tech growth, compared to just 24% of U.S.
    • The survey found a significant gap between the U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Wealthy Europeans are looking to alternative asset classes to build exposure to artificial intelligence themes amid turbulence in public markets.

    According to recent reports, goldman Sachs Alternatives' inaugural survey of high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth investors found 47% of European respondents saw alternatives as the best way to gain exposure to AI and future tech growth, compared to just 24% of U.S. investors.

    The survey found a significant gap between the U.S. and Europe in terms of investor knowledge of alternatives, which include assets like private equity, property and infrastructure. Goldman noted 82% of European respondents are familiar with the alternative investments market — compared to 50% of U.S. investors.

    Goldman polled 1,000 investors with at least 1 million in investable assets in their local currency across the U.K., France, Germany, Italy and Switzerland. The survey was carried out between June 29 and Aug. 18 this year.

    The report on the findings, published Wednesday, did not specify the proportion of respondents who already have a stake in some kind of alternative investment — but wealthy Europeans appeared particularly bullish on the space.

    Private equity made up the largest proportion of current alternatives holdings. Among wealthy Europeans with alternatives exposure, 62% noted they invested in private equity. The second most commonly held asset class was private real estate, which was backed by 51% of European alternatives investors. Hedge funds were held by 37% of European alternatives owners, and private infrastructure was held by 30%.

    One in four respondents who did not already own an alternative investment stated they were likely to invest in the market in the coming 12 months. Among those already in the space, 26% said they were likely to increase their allocations over the next year, while just 5% said they planned to decrease their exposure.

    Of the European investors who already owned alternatives, 54% stated their assets had performed as expected, while 44% said their assets had exceeded their expectations to the upside. Only 2% said their alternative investments had performed worse than expected.

    "Recent reforms gave individual investors unprecedented access to alternative asset classes like private equity, venture capital, and private credit," Kyle Kniffen, global head of alternatives for third-party wealth at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, remarked in Wednesday's report.

    He added that wealthy investors "look ready to jump at the opportunity.".

    "Our survey reveals satisfaction among current alts owners is high and adoption looks set to increase," Kniffen remarked.

    Alternative investments have increasingly become a staple of high-net-worth individuals' investment portfolios.

    Over the past year, JPMorgan Asset Management's private wealth alternative assets in the Asia-Pacific region have jumped 40%, while BNY Wealth notes alternative investments now account for 60% of single-family office portfolios — recently surpassing traditional assets for the first time.

    In a recent development, but investing in alternatives carries risks. Private equity, for example, can lock up capital for long periods, and although the number of exits ticked slightly higher last year, the value of those deals fell.

    Concerns about private credit, meanwhile, have dominated headlines, with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon warning on Oct. 14, 2025, that "cockroaches" were likely to be lurking in private markets.

    — CNBC's Lee Ying Shan contributed to this article.

    Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

    ⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur.
    • Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.
    • But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

    Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

    But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

    The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

    The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their major-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

    There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

    Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

    Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

    “He is a top player, no doubt about it,” said head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

    “He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”.

    Sources indicate that A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

    Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

    Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh.

    Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

    Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

    He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

    Richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

    Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

    Sources indicate that vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ.

    De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

    This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

    Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

    Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

    Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU.

    Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

    Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h.

    De Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will quickly look a lot different. There are more new faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

    Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

    But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

    Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that major-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his latest-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

    Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on new players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

    Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

    Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

    In a recent development, his team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian stated: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

    According to recent reports, “You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

    “We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a newly introduced project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

    Industry observers note that “I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

    “Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

    “We can improve promptly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] new players but we have to put something more.

    “We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve swiftly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an notable defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”.

    We had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

    It has been revealed that it was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. To become a team I mentioned before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

    In a recent development, it was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

    Sources indicate that we didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

    Sources indicate that really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can quickly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

    In a recent development, our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

    Sources indicate that that’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

    He’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so quickly.

    Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

    According to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

    Less Christ the Redeemer more Christ, that was terrible.

    "I think that sums it up"Fair to say this Spurs fan wasn't pleased with their performance 😅 pic.twitter.com/ZAdVaVbjlS.

    Possibly Brentford’s best performance under Keith Andrews, though that may be overstating the strength of the opposition. This was a complete display: they pressed Spurs, they played through Spurs, they played over Spurs, they dominated Spurs from set-pieces and their defenders bullied Spurs’s forwards. It will be interesting to hear from De Zerbi and whether he is philosophical or irate. This is far from Spurs’s ideal projected team, but still unacceptable.

    Kinsky palms away a Damsgaard corner, and Yarmoliuk slices his shot over the bar. We are deep into stoppage time, and Brentford’s players are still pressing Bentnacur and Senesi and making them play with their heads down.

    Sources indicate that just four minutes of added time to play but Spurs have more defending to do in the shape over another Brentford corner. They survive, but Brentford swiftly establish possession again.

    It would appear Lord Sugar is still watching:.

    According to recent reports, to all Spurs fans don't worry this is all tactical to lure other teams into believing we are a easy touch. #coys.

    It has been revealed that another Brentford debut: Callum Wilson replaces Igor Thiago. Destiny Udogie has replaced Archie Gray for Spurs. “You should have signed for a massive club!” sing the Brentford fans, in reference to the club almost signing Gray two summers ago. Football fans never forget.

    Another Brentford goal would put them top of the table, for what that is worth. Spurs enjoying some possession in the Brentford half now, but it is entirely sterile.

    Igor Thiago’s shot is blocked, Brentford still look the more likely team to score the next goal. Jadon Anthony indicates he has a long throw, which might be a small reason why Brentford decided to sign him. Janelt then drags back Maddison.

    In a recent development, jadon Anthony involved in some Brenford pressure that results in a long throw and a corner, but the new man then slices a volley over the bar. Standing ovation at the Gtech for Sangare as he makes way for Damsgaard, while Hickey replaces Kayode. Be tough to beat his performance as debut of the weekend.

    Michael Oliver letting some meaty challenges go, the game is quite feisty despite the scoreline. Schade released himself into a tackle on Solanke but he did not really catch him with his studs.

    A few Spurs fans may have thought better of staying to watch the final 20 minutes. I wonder “if” this Spurs fan has switched the television off?

    Industry observers note that first match if season . Smiling before the game. Hope to be smiling after. pic.twitter.com/hsTc79PBti.

    Recent findings suggest that richarlison beats the turf and Ajer punches the air after the Brentford defender wins the foul. Andrews is making another couple of changes: Jensen and Ouattara off, Yarmoliuk and upcoming signing Jadon Anthony on.

    Two more Spurs changes too: Maddison and Solanke on, Moore and Richarlison off.

    Really sharp save from Kelleher to keep out Moore’s powerful shot from close range. Moore has at least carried a threat for Spurs in the second half, but they are struggling to sustain much pressure.

    Industry observers note that tonali with a hit from 25 yards but it deflects comfortably into the arms of Kelleher. Surely a (Kew?) bridge too far for Spurs to dig out any kind of result from here.

    De Zerbi looks a little resigned on the touchline, he will know that this is far from his ideal Spurs team on the pitch but that cannot excuse such poor standards.

    Recent findings suggest that he fails to open his account for the season. Sent Kinsky the wrong way, but he dragged the penalty just a touch and it cannoned off the post. The lead remains three.

    Recent findings suggest that igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h.

    Spurs are being overpowered here, they cannot cope whenever Brentford come forward. There were appeals for handball against Van Hecke after Janelt swivelled and shot, but the foul is given against Bentancur for bundling over Schade. A complete mess for Spurs.

    Any hope that the half-time double change would bring a revival now appear forlorn.

    But here is a chance for Mikey Moore! Robertson forward to good effect, and his low cross arrives to Moore at the back post but his shot was too close to Kelleher. Almost crept through his legs.

Cracking strike from Sangare from the edge of the box after a Brentford corner is cleared, they have always been so good at winning those second balls. Driven strike, good save from Kinsky and Kayode is first to the rebound to score from a couple of yards.

    Recent findings suggest that this has been a dreadful start to the season by Tottenham. Sandro Tonali has barely looked like a £10m player, let alone a £100m midfielder and, maybe unsurprisingly, De Zerbi’s players look like strangers. He will demand a major improvement in the second half. Keith Andrews will be delighted - maybe other than the fact the game isn’t already dead. His team have been dominant.

    In a recent development, brentford utterly dominant, there has been an alarming gulf in industry, precision and class between the two teams. Spurs will surely improve, both in the second half and as the season goes on, but this has fallen well below the standards you expect of a team with European aspirations. If a few of these players never played for De Zerbi again they could have no complaints.

    It has been revealed that no sign of a Spurs revival at half time, Brentford playing through their press with ease and then have space to run into. Kayode wins his header at the back post but no player was there for the knockdown.

    Vital block from Ajer after Spurs’s best piece of combination play around the box, before Tonali slashes a volley well over the bar from distance. Cue “what a waste of money” from the home fans.

    Richarlison has been non-existent up front for Spurs, bullied by Collins and Ajer.

    Sources indicate that lewis-Potter swings in a dangerous cross, headed down by Kayode, and Van Hecke stoops to block Outtara’s shot. The whistle goes for a high boot.

Spurs caught in that Brentford man-to-man press again and the ball bounces off Richarlison.     Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ.

    Spurs’s defence breached again, and Outtara really should have made it two but his first touch was far too heavy and Kinsky was able to clear. Spurs will not be the only team to struggle against this Brentford front three. Schade won the flick on, Thiago swept the ball across the box, but the finish was lacking from Outtara.

    According to recent reports, outtara fouls his former Bournemouth team-mate in the Spurs box. Then Brentford win a free-kick which will go in the mixer. Senesi fouled Outtara.

    Brentford continue to look the better team, moving the ball at pace in the final third, but Schade stumbles up against Bergvall in the box. Spurs yet to settle of establish any possession in the game so far.

    From that free-kick, Jenson’s delivery was a wicked one: inswinging and flat to the near post, and the ball glanced off Robertson’s head and behind for a corner.

    Jensen then tees up Lewis-Potter for an ambitious volley from the edge of the box, and there are hopeful appeals for a handball penalty against Gallagher, and then Collins fails to divert to follow up cross on target.

    Spurs under some pressure early on.

    Not the most distinctive contrast between the two kits, but not as bad as Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen in pre-season.

    Brentford on the front foot in the early exchanges, Sangare involve in their first attack, but Tel runs back to defend well against Kayode.

    Schade then wins a free-kick from Van Hecke in a crossing position wide left, the forward’s feet were too quick for the Dutch defender.

    The usual rendition of Hey Jude before the game in south west London.

    [On three of the back four being newly introduced signings] I have a significant confidence because all three are very important players with experience and qualities. They have been working for one month and we have no problem with them.

    According to recent reports, there’s a decent chance this Tottenham starting line-up will not play again together for the rest of this season. Mikey Moore is expected to move to Cologne on loan, while Savinho’s arrival will relegate Mathys Tel to the bench. Spurs also have Mohamed Kudus and Xavi Simons to return from injury. De Zerbi will want a good start to the season, but this is not the Tottenham side he will be relying upon moving forwards.

    According to recent reports, there will be no easing into life at Spurs for Robertson, who faces Dango Outtara in one of the game’s key duels. The Scot has plenty of experience of course, but there were signs towards the end of time at Liverpool that he had started to struggle in one-on-ones against wingers.

    Archie Gray will become Tottenham’s youngest-ever captain tonight. Aged 20 years and 163 days, he will beat Steve Perryman’s record of 20 years and 260 days. On Friday, De Zerbi listed all of his captains with Gray down in fifth place. Latest permanent captain Micky van de Ven misses the trip to Brentford through injury.

    It has been revealed that if we include the league goals Mikey Moore scored while on loan at Rangers last season, Spurs’s front three scored 22 league goals combined last season. By contrast, Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara scored 37 between them in the Premier League. Brentford are firm favourites with the bookies for this one, and that difference in firepower is probably why. Omar Marmoush could help matters.

    Recent findings suggest that seventeen-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett is one of the outstanding players in the country at his age group, and there is a lot of excitement about him at Spurs. Post-Kane, the club’s academy has not delivered much bona fide first-team quality, but Williams-Barnett appears on that trajectory.

    Subs: Dubravka, Danso, Maddison, Udogie, Fernandes, Solanke, Bentancur, Davies, Williams-Barnett.

    Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

    It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

    Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

    Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the significant spenders.

    Recent findings suggest that that is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s fresh leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

    The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

    De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

    According to recent reports, spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

    Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

    Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the substantial boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

    Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

    In a recent development, “He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”.

    Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Thanksgiving is a huge day in the NFL with three games stacked throughout.
    • Thursday's slate of games was overshadowed by coverage of Aaron Rodgers' rant on Wednesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show," with pregame analysts from both CBS and Fox calling out his message and how he delivered it.
    • Former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Terry Bradshaw did not mince words on the Fox broadcast ahead of the Philadelphia Eagles taking on the Dallas Cowboys.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Thanksgiving is a huge day in the NFL with three games stacked throughout.

    Thursday's slate of games was overshadowed by coverage of Aaron Rodgers' rant on Wednesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show," with pregame analysts from both CBS and Fox calling out his message and how he delivered it.

    Former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Terry Bradshaw did not mince words on the Fox broadcast ahead of the Philadelphia Eagles taking on the Dallas Cowboys.

    "I'm sorry that Aaron Rodgers had to do this. I'm sorry that he had to go public with all of his gripes and complaints. Am I surprised? Absolutely not. In my opinion, he is a strange guy anyway.

    "The one thing you don't do … none of us turn on our teammates, we don't turn on our coaching staff, we don't turn on our ownership. We show class on the way out, Aaron Rodgers didn't do that.

    "I'm reminded he said, 'When I'm through playing here in Pittsburgh, I'll disappear and you'll never hear or see from me again.'.

    "And I hope this is one time he is telling the truth.".

    He wasn't the only former Steelers quarterback-turned-analyst who weighed in. Russell Wilson gave his two cents on the CBS pregame show ahead of the Chicago Bears-Detroit Lions game, but focused more on what this means for Rodgers' legacy and called it a disappointment.

    It has been revealed that "We've all been in the room. Like, we've seen coaches fall asleep in moments — long days, long hours. We've seen players fall asleep in moments. ... The reality is Aaron Rodgers wanted to call the plays, right? And that's the difference here. ... The reality is the ultimatum was the ultimatum. ... If not, I want my release, essentially. And so they made that decision. ...

    "It's about Aaron Rodgers' legacy. ... If I'm his family members, if I'm somebody close to him, I'm his significant other, whatever it may be: 'Is this how you want to go out?' After all the success he's had, is this how you want to go out?... This is a disappointment.".

    On the Fox pregame show, Hall of Famer Michael Strahan talked about Rodgers' situation. He admitted McCarthy probably isn't innocent in this scenario, but he focused his analysis on the impact Rodgers' rant had on the Steelers.

    "What's disappointing to me is that you hurt your team. It's about the team. We are playing a team sport, which you cannot play as an individual. And that's what he's doing, he's an individual in a team game, and it does not work if your attitude is not right.

    Sources indicate that "You can be a narcissist and play football, but hold it in when it's something to say. Always let the coach win in public. In private, you handle your business with your coach.

    "One thing I hated to see was him saying, 'I can speak about it now, I made $400 million.' You're a rich jerk. You're a rich, bad teammate.".

    Rodgers was released hours after his rant Wednesday. He cleared waivers on Thursday and is a free agent able to sign with any team.

    That may be easier said than done, though, as ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that at least one AFC exec said about the quarterback finding a fresh landing spot: "Teams desperate on the playoff bubble, maybe, but it's going to be hard after watching him go scorched-earth on people and an organization like that.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The UAE is "very optimistic" about achieving 7%-8% growth next year, the country's economy and tourism minister Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri told CNBC after the latest data from the International Monetary Fund showed the country would avoid a recession in 2026.

    Industry observers note that the IMF last week revised the UAE's real GDP forecast to 0.2% growth in 2026 from a 3.9% contraction predicted a month ago. "The UAE is coming back, and that adjustment within one month indicates that there is a huge potential aspect when it comes towards the end of the year," the minister told CNBC's Dan Murphy.

    He mentioned the tourism industry was already picking up with occupancy rates returning to "almost near normal" and international carriers including British Airways and Air France rerouting flights to the UAE. The minister expects economic growth to be higher than 0.2% this year.

    The Iran war has disrupted economic activity in the UAE, with missile and drone attacks from Tehran and maritime disruptions weighing on energy trade, tourism, aviation and private-sector confidence.

    Earlier this month, U.S. President Donald Trump stated that renewed attacks on Iran were "highly unlikely" if negotiations produce a "very strong agreement." However, on Monday, Trump threatened that Tehran could face fresh U.S. strikes next year if the two countries failed to strike a deal, as per Fox News.

    "We can we cannot promise the world for any storms that will land on our shore, but we can always promise that the UAE's economy is ready for any storm," Al Marri said.

    He added that next year the UAE's economy will have a "different" model than the one before the conflict and investments will be focused on building factories and "things that we really need in times of crisis.".

    The World Bank in October said it expects the UAE's economy to recover next year, driven by rising oil production and exports and a rebound in tourism, trade, transportation, financial services, and construction.

    It warned that the improvement in economic activity in the UAE largely depends on the duration and intensity of the Iran war, with a faster de-escalation likely to accelerate the recovery in services exports and private-sector activity.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the firm "has its own China problem.".
    • Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.
    • It has been revealed that the report claims that "after the U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the firm "has its own China problem.".

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

    It has been revealed that the report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the firm kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Hunterbrook also mentioned that new export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

    It has been revealed that the allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

    "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson remarked in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    Norse Atlantic suspends all flights, warns it may file for bankruptcy after share price collapse

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (538 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Norse Atlantic suspended all of its flights on Thursday and warned it may have to file for bankruptcy after its stock collapsed on Wednesday following its warning about its "critical" financial situation.
    • Oslo-listed shares of Norse closed 85% lower on Wednesday.
    • In a recent development, "The board of directors continues to consider options to secure short-term financing," Norse remarked in a Thursday statement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Norse Atlantic suspended all of its flights on Thursday and warned it may have to file for bankruptcy after its stock collapsed on Wednesday following its warning about its "critical" financial situation.

    Oslo-listed shares of Norse closed 85% lower on Wednesday.

    In a recent development, "The board of directors continues to consider options to secure short-term financing," Norse remarked in a Thursday statement. "If a short-term financing solution is not secured urgently, it is the board's intention to file for bankruptcy.".

    The airline added that "there can be no assurance that a viable solution will be found.".

    Checks by CNBC highlighted the airline was still selling tickets for flights on Friday and beyond as of 9 a.m. Oslo time on Thursday.

    Warning signs first popped up when PK786 from London to Islamabad and PK710 from Manchester to Lahore were cancelled because of "an unexpected operational suspension," the Pakistani flag carrier mentioned on X.

    Industry observers note that the airline had been set to operate two Pakistan International Airlines flights Wednesday under a wet-lease agreement, in which one airline provides the aircraft and crew to another. The agreement had only been signed in early October.

    PIA stated it would operate the routes using its own Boeing 777 aircraft from the next day.

    Norse's own flight Z0 783 from London Gatwick to Orlando was also shown as canceled Wednesday on live air traffic website Flightradar24. London Gatwick's website listed the flight's status for Thursday as "enquire airline.".

    In a bid to stave off financial troubles, Norse cut 75 jobs in May as part of an effort to reduce costs by $50 million, after Eivind Roald replaced founder Bjorn Tore Larsen as CEO in November last year.

    The Norwegian carrier remarked Wednesday that its situation depended on securing financing for short-term liquidity needs and that it was in discussions about a potential strategic takeover.

    "Norse is also engaged in discussions with selected parties on short term financing, however, there can be no assurances that such discussions will result in a viable solution," the airline mentioned.

    The Norwegian carrier has come under strain due to soaring jet fuel costs since the onset of the Iran war.

    India's largest airline, low-cost carrier IndiGo, entered an agreement with Norse Atlantic in early 2025 to lease six 787-9 aircraft as it launched flights to Europe and Britain ahead of the arrival of its own widebody planes.

    The agreement concluded at the end of October this year, with IndiGo citing airspace constraints, elevated fuel costs and currency pressures.

    It has been revealed that at its peak in 2024, Norse Atlantic had 4,822 scheduled flights. That number dipped to 4,695 in 2025 and 2,565 in 2026, according to aviation analytics firm Cirium. The airline had 122 flights scheduled for November this year.

    Norse Atlantic CEO Roald told CNBC in May that he was not "overly concerned" about access to fuel and remarked the airline had no indication at the time that the crisis would have an immediate impact. The airline said in October that it was continuing to operate at reduced capacity because of "prolonged high fuel prices.".

    Correction: This story was updated to reflect that Norse shares closed 85% lower on Wednesday.

    Phoenix Suns guard Dillon Brooks and Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant exchanged words at the end of Houston's 116-104 win on Wednesday night.

    Durant was chippy all night, making sure to deliver extra trash talk against his former team.

    Recent findings suggest that with less than 30 seconds left in the game, the Rockets led by 10. In a wild moment, Durant and Brooks weren't really playing; they were just talking to each other near halfcourt while the action continued.

    Houston's Fred VanVleet hit a jumper with 23.8 seconds left to make it a 114-102 game in the Rockets' favor. Brooks and Durant were chirping at each other and got in each other's faces.

    Industry observers note that the referees assessed each player a technical foul. Because Brooks had received a technical foul earlier in the quarter with 4:32 left, he was ejected. VanVleet drained a three and motioned to Brooks; they chirped and were both assessed technicals.

    Recent findings suggest that durant finished the game with 20 points and 10 rebounds. With 46.3 seconds left in the second quarter, the veteran forward drained a 3-pointer. That basket helped him become the fifth player in NBA history to score at least 33,000 points. He joins LeBron James (43,672 and counting), Kareem Abdul-Jabbar (38,387), Karl Malone (36,298) and Kobe Bryant (33,643).

    The win moved Houston to 14-5. The Rockets return to action Saturday, hosting the Philadelphia 76ers.

    The loss dropped Phoenix to 9-8. The Suns had won four straight before Wednesday's loss, and now turn their attention to taking on the Dallas Mavericks on Friday night.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang is back at the helm of Nvidia — and Denny's has a booth waiting for him.

    Recent findings suggest that the American diner chain welcomed the billionaire's return as Nvidia CEO by revealing that it had reinstated a commemorative plaque marking the birthplace of the artificial intelligence chip giant after learning of its removal on Nov. 13.

    According to recent reports, "Some things you just don't take off the menu. Jensen Huang is one of them," Denny's stated in a post on X.

    The plaque marks the booth at a Denny's restaurant in Silicon Valley, California, where Huang and his co-founders discussed the idea for Nvidia, which was founded in 1993.

    The restaurant chain stated it learned on Nov. 13, a day after Huang's resignation, that the plaque had been removed.

    "We put the plaque right back up where it belongs," Denny's mentioned, without specifying who had removed it or why.

    Huang's ties to the diner chain, however, stretch back well before Nvidia's founding. He worked at Denny's as a teenager, washing dishes and serving customers before going on to build one of the world's most valuable companies.

    Sources indicate that the restaurant chain also disclosed that it had contacted Nvidia's communications team on Nov. 10 to express its pride in their shared history.

    Huang's return came less than two weeks after his sudden resignation rattled investors and raised questions about corporate governance and succession planning at the chipmaker.

    While his return has put those problems in the spotlight, Denny's offered a simpler message to its former employee.

    "Jensen, your booth is waiting and the coffee's on. We're always open, 24/7," the restaurant chain noted.

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (456 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Switzerland’s biggest bank set for showdown with lawmakers as capital fight intensifies amid crisis planning

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (456 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that UBS's crisis planning has won qualified support from market regulators, which called its plan "executable" in principle.
    • FINMA, the Swiss markets regulator, noted Wednesday that UBS's resolvability — or its ability to fail safely, without wreaking havoc on the economy — has improved since it integrated rival Credit Suisse, with progress made in implementing the emergency initiative across group-wide resolution planning.
    • The preferred resolution strategy — involving looks to allow for recapitalization and restructuring through the use of loss-absorbing bail-in bonds — is "executable," FINMA noted.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that UBS's crisis planning has won qualified support from market regulators, which called its plan "executable" in principle. But Switzerland's biggest bank still faces a major fight over sweeping plans that would force it to hold more capital against its foreign subsidiaries.

    FINMA, the Swiss markets regulator, noted Wednesday that UBS's resolvability — or its ability to fail safely, without wreaking havoc on the economy — has improved since it integrated rival Credit Suisse, with progress made in implementing the emergency initiative across group-wide resolution planning.

    The preferred resolution strategy — involving looks to allow for recapitalization and restructuring through the use of loss-absorbing bail-in bonds — is "executable," FINMA noted. The regulator formally approved UBS's recovery initiative for the first time since its ​Credit Suisse integration.

    How UBS would withstand a future crisis remains in sharp focus among Swiss authorities ever since the lender's emergency takeover of stricken rival Credit Suisse in 2023.

    UBS is now the country's only global systemically vital bank, and the Swiss government wants it to hold stronger capital cushions, specifically in relation to its foreign subsidiaries, which would help it withstand another banking collapse.

    UBS has pushed back against the overhaul, saying the measures are disproportionate and would damage its international competitiveness, forcing it to hold an extra $16 billion in capital.

    Recent findings suggest that A parliamentary showdown now looms, with the National Council, Switzerland's lower house, scheduled to debate the proposal Dec. 16.

    According to recent reports, on Tuesday, the lower house's economics committee backed aims to force the bank to support its foreign subsidiaries with 90% high-quality core Common Equity Tier 1, or CET1, capital. The Council of States, the country's upper house, approved the 90% initiative in September.

    Recent findings suggest that the Swiss government had earlier proposed a 100% threshold. UBS wants it to be no more than 50%.

    According to recent reports, UBS CEO Sergio Ermotti told CNBC in an interview Oct. 28 that 90% would not allow the company to be a "competitive player" long-term. But he would not be drawn on speculation that the measures could push the bank to relocate out of Switzerland.

    In a statement, the bank said the economics committee's recommendation would herald further excessive tightening of Swiss capital requirements, "which are already among the most stringent globally.".

    It has been revealed that FINMA mentioned in its Nov. 25 update that the goal is to avoid government solvency support and emergency law.

    "The aim is to enable the authorities, in the event of a crisis, to choose the option that offers the best prospects of success in safeguarding financial stability and ensuring the continuation of systemically notable functions," the regulator stated.

    #143462. What is ‘texture-maxxing’? The food trend putting crunch on the menu

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (472 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    What is ‘texture-maxxing’? The food trend putting crunch on the menu

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (472 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Texture-maxxing is the latest food trend taking social media by storm as consumers, driven by aesthetics and taste, look for a sensory experience.
    • British supermarket Waitrose's latest food and drink report highlighted "texture-maxxing" as one of the trends of the year.
    • According to recent reports, "This year, the sound of food went mainstream," Waitrose's Senior Development Chef Will Torrent said in the Wednesday report.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Texture-maxxing is the latest food trend taking social media by storm as consumers, driven by aesthetics and taste, look for a sensory experience.

    British supermarket Waitrose's latest food and drink report highlighted "texture-maxxing" as one of the trends of the year. It describes the phenomenon as a multi-sensory indulgence that is "fuelled by texture-maxxing crunch and intense flavour hits," pushing shoppers to fill their trolleys with crunchy peanut butter, dumplings, and trifles.

    According to recent reports, "This year, the sound of food went mainstream," Waitrose's Senior Development Chef Will Torrent said in the Wednesday report. "Driven by social media's obsession with audible, multi-sensory cooking, we're creating high-contrast meals that combine shatter-crisp crunch with pillowy chew.".

    "The emphasis in social media content has flipped from narrative voiceovers to ASMR-inspired audio, where the evocative sounds of food are just as notable as the visuals," he added.

    It has been revealed that food trends on social media have ranged from the obvious to the absurd. Fibermaxxing and proteinmaxxing have taken off in the past few years. Meanwhile, food and beverages like Dubai chocolate, protein coffee, and ube were some of the major social media hits.

    Nestlé's USA 2026 trends found that 75% of Gen Z and 80% of millennials sought out texture in snack cravings with the hashtag "crunchtok," amassing 1.5 billion views.

    Waitrose noted that shoppers looking to maximize on texture bought its viral No.1 Alphonso Mango Dessert, which involves "cracking through the crisp shell" to access a "smooth mango mousse and passion fruit curd on a crunchy white chocolate base.".

    According to recent reports, waitrose's TikTok and Instagram videos of eating the dessert were watched by more than two million people, with a whopping 6,173 hours and 36 minutes of play time on TikTok. Its videos featuring crunchy toast also went viral.

    The U.K. grocer's sales of jarred chili crunches, which include crispy rayu oils such as itsu Crispy Chilli Oil, saw a 13-fold jump. Meanwhile, crunchy peanut butter outsold smooth.

    Dumplings also had a moment, with sales of chicken gyoza dumplings up 116% this year and searches on waitrose.com for gochujang and peanut butter udon noodles jumped 60%.

    "We've seen an explosion in demand as shoppers treat dumplings not just as a quick weeknight bite, but as a total sensory experience," Waitrose's Executive Chef Stephen Parkins-Knight noted.

    "Driven by the rise of texture-maxxing, people want that ultimate contrast: delicate skins, juicy fillings and crispy skirts, topped with very chilli crunch. With innovation ranging from fusion fillings to rich dipping broths, dumplings have taken a delicious centre stage in 2026," he added.

    Texture-maxxing also extended to desserts, as shoppers bought twice as many chocolate trifles compared to 2025, and sales of strawberry trifles increased 160%.

    Tiramisu was also popular, with searches for waitrose.com's tiramisu recipe page increasing 155% year-on-year.

    #143459. Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (745 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (745 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S.
    • The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a massive win for the manufacturer and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    Industry observers note that some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    Recent findings suggest that adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and mentioned it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the substantial indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    According to recent reports, "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he noted.

    Part of the challenge, Niles said, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    Sources indicate that "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," stated JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he remarked, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    Sources indicate that anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan said. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the company in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he mentioned. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    One bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.
